titleStmt.title: Memorandum from the Secretary of State to the President

keywords.term: Goodpaster, Brigadier General Andrew J., Jr.

div.head: PM–22. Memorandum from the Secretary of State to the President

list.label: SUBJECT
list.item: Recommendation That You Sign A Letter To President de la Guardia of Panama.

div.p: In view of the decisions taken at your October 12 meeting on United States-Panamanian relations, which has resulted in revisions in certain operating policies of the Canal Zone authorities, I recommend that you approve the enclosed letter addressed to President Ernesto de la Guardia of Panama.

The proposed message refers to a meeting on September 1, 1959 of United States and Panamanian representatives in which President de la Guardia actively participated. At that time steps were discussed which would help minimize certain sources of friction between our two countries. As a result of your October 12 meeting, the Canal Zone authorities have begun to take the necessary action to implement the steps discussed at the September 1 meeting, i.e. that the Zone revise the third country purchasing practices, and that luxury item sales through Zone outlets be limited insofar as possible. This information would be conveyed orally to the Panamanian President at the time of delivery of your letter by our Ambassador. Information on other contemplated
actions would be communicated to the Panamanian Government at the appropriate time.

Moreover, I feel it important for us to have a communication setting forth your personal interests in our relations with Panama, for should Panama [illegible in the original] its allegations of our non-compliance with the 1955 Treaty before the International Court of Justice continue in the future, the United States would have a written record of our good faith in cooperating with Panama in the efforts to increase its participation in the [illegible in the original] and [illegible in the original] of the Canal Zone.

In order to derive appropriate [illegible in the original] from our [illegible in the original] the bar of world public opinion, [illegible in the original] what this message, if approved, be released as soon as it has been delivered to President de la Guardia. If this is agreeable, the Department will instruct Embassy Panama to report delivery so that immediate public release may be made by the White House.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Central Files, 611.19/10–2859. Confidential. Drafted by Sharp.

In a letter dated September 4, 1959, Ambassador Harrington informed Deputy Assistant Secretary of State William P. Snow of the details of the meeting on September 1 and the decisions taken. (ARA/OAP Files, Lot 64 D 67, “Panama Relations. August–September 1959”)

According to a typewritten note on the source text, Goodpaster informed officials of the Executive Secretariat on October 29 that the President had approved without change the suggested letter to President de la Guardia. An additional handwritten notation on the source text indicated that the signed original of this letter had been received from the White House on November 2 and had been transmitted.
